data.long_meaning: Someone who is discontent and detached from the material world, often in search of spiritual enlightenment. The name Maznun carries the meaning “The Discontent” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Parents who choose Maznun usually hope their child will grow to embody the discontent and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Maznun belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The Discontent.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maznun total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_urdu.name: مزنون
in_urdu.meaning: مزنون عمر کے بالغ شخص جو کچھ نہیں سمجھتا
in_urdu.long_meaning: مزنون عمر کے بالغ شخص جو کچھ نہیں سمجھتا، دین کے بارے میں کچھ نہیں جانتا، اللہ کا عبادت نہیں کرتا، نہ ہی ان کے پاس ان کی طرف سے کوئی عقیدہ ہے، نہ ہی وہ اپنے رسول کی اطاعت کرتے ہیں، نہ ہی وہ قرآن کی پڑھائی میں عقیدہ رکھتے ہیں، وہ دنیا میں زہد نہیں کرتے، نہ ہی ان کے پاس آخرت کے بارے میں کوئی عقیدہ ہے، وہ علم سے فائدہ نہیں اٹھاتے، نہ ہی ان کے پاس رزق کے بارے میں کوئی عقیدہ ہے، وہ جنت میں زہد نہیں کرتے، نہ ہی ان کے پاس دوزخ کے بارے میں کوئی عقیدہ ہے

data.cultural_impact: The name Maznun holds cultural significance in Islamic tradition, particularly in reference to the life and story of a famous figure known as Al-Maznun AL-Ansari. He was a well-known ascetic who renounced worldly possessions and lived a life of extreme asceticism and solitude. His story has been passed down through generations, inspiring many to seek spiritual enlightenment and detachment from material desires.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spirituality, the attribute of Maznun holds great spiritual significance as it represents the ideal of detachment from worldly desires and a complete focus on the pursuit of spiritual growth. It is a reminder of the transient nature of material possessions and the importance of striving for a deeper connection with the Divine. This detachment frees the soul from the chains of worldly distractions, allowing it to soar in the realm of the spiritual.
